messages:
Maya (Support): FYI — opened customer ticket (Acme) asking for a way to receive partially streamed structured fn-call outputs to their webhook. They want schema validation on each partial frame and explicit 'final' marker.
Sam (Product): Can you paste the ticket text? Is this about chat+fncall streaming or the /completions stream we have?
Maya (Support): Chat + fn_call. Excerpt: "We need to start ingesting incremental JSON fragments as we get them — validate each fragment against our schema and optionally ack. We also need to be able to resume if we miss a frame."
Ravi (Sales): This came up in our demo today. They consider this high priority for onboarding (banking workflows). If we don't ship we'll lose a PoC.
Dev (Eng): Implementation notes: we currently stream token deltas. Adding frame-level structured events is feasible but touches runtime framing and webhook delivery. We need: 1) output event envelope, 2) per-frame schema URL/hashes, 3) resumable cursors (seq ids), 4) finalization event.
Sam (Product): OK — propose we treat this as a product spike -> scoped feature. Draft acceptance criteria: (a) SDK + REST streaming deliver events of type 'frame' and 'final', (b) frames include "seq_id" and optional "schema_id", (c) webhook delivery retries preserve order and support idempotency, (d) docs/examples for verifying schema hashes, (e) compatibility mode for older clients to receive full consolidated JSON.
Maya (Support): Customer also asked for per-frame validation failure behavior: either drop+send error frame or stop the stream. They preferred an explicit error frame with path info.
Dev (Eng): We should avoid breaking customers. Default behavior: send an ERROR frame with {seq_id, errors: [...], action: "continue"|"abort"}. Make abort opt-in via request param.
Ravi (Sales): Pricing question: streaming partial frames increases request count semantics. We need a clear billing model before marketing. Recommend: bill by token + framing overhead negligible, but add a flag for 'frame_count' visibility in console.
Sam (Product): Prioritization: this maps to security/regulatory customers plus integrations team. Ask: is this Critical or High? Proposed: High — ship in next quarter as Beta for dedicated/private customers, GA later.
Maya (Support): Can we commit to a pilot for Acme? They'll accept Beta in Dedicated.
Dev (Eng): Rough engineering estimate: 3-week spike + 4 weeks to productize (webhook delivery plumbing, idempotency, tests, docs). Unknowns: how resume tokens map to existing KV cache and how it affects batching.
Sam (Product): Action items: @Dev (Eng) run a 2-week spike to validate resume + framing; @Maya (Support) get exact schema and P0 customer acceptance criteria; @Ravi (Sales) confirm commercial terms for Beta. We'll discuss rollout gating: perf < 200ms per-frame median, successful resume tests, and clear billing.
Maya (Support): I'll upload the ticket payload and sample schema to the handoff doc. Also confirm they want HMAC for frame authenticity.
Dev (Eng): Note to self: possible framing envelope prototype: ```
{"type":"frame","seq_id":123,"schema_id":"sha256:...","payload":{...}}
{"type":"error","seq_id":124,"errors":[{"path":"items[0].amount","msg":"expected number"}],"action":"continue"}
{"type":"final","seq_id":150,"summary":{...}}
```
Ravi (Sales): If we can promise per-frame HMAC and resume tokens, legal will be happier. I'll flag to the AE.
Sam (Product): Decision: create a roadmap epic "streaming structured frames + resumability" with priority High. Beta scope: dedicated/private only, opt-in param `streaming=framed`. GA scope to evaluate after telemetry.
infra-bot: Created issue RW-17834: streaming-framed-outputs (epic).
Maya (Support): Thanks — I'll ping Acme to confirm Beta timeline and will attach their schema.
Sam (Product): Scheduling note: add this to next weekly roadmap sync. If spike shows major infra changes, we may re-scope.
Dev (Eng): Added initial spike checklist to the issue. Will post findings 2 weeks from today.
Maya (Support): Final: Customer asked for sample SDK snippet for verifying frames. I'll request acceptance test vectors so we can ship with example code.
Sam (Product): Great — closing thread for now, will follow up in epic comments. :thumbsup:
